messages.subject: The Subbotin (Exponential Power) Distribution
parts:
Hi all, 

I have a quick question how to define arbitrary posterior distribution in Stan. I wan to define the Subbotin or exponential power distribution in my model, which is not already defined in Stan to my best knowledge. The pdf of the Subottin distribution is y =    with three parameters \alpha, \beta, and \mu. Any help will be highly appreciated!

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] The Subbotin (Exponential Power) Distribution
parts:
Hi Jangho,

This one's easy. I'm not familiar with the distribution and I don't know the effect of having a discontinuity at mu == x, but this one's easy to code up:

functions {
  real subottin_log(real x, real alpha, real beta, real mu) {
     real y;
     y <- beta / (2 * alpha * exp(lgamma(1 / beta)) * exp(-pow(abs(x - mu) / alpha, beta)));
     return log(y);
  }
}

I didn't actually run it, so if there are typos, it might not compile. This isn't the most efficient code out there. Stan has the lgamma function, so I took the exp of the lgamma function, but if it'd be better if you worked directly in log space.

If you did that, inside the model block, you could do something like...

   x ~ subottin(alpha, beta, mu)

where any of those could be data or parameters.



Daniel

functions 
{
real subottin_log(real x, real alpha, real beta, real mu) {
real y;

y <- beta / (2 * alpha * exp(lgamma(1 / beta)) * exp(-pow(fabs(y - mu) / alpha, beta)));
return log(y);
  }
}
data{
int<lower=0> N;
real y[N];
}
parameters{
real mu;
real alpha;
real<lower=0> beta;

model{
y~subottin(alpha,beta,mu);

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] The Subbotin (Exponential Power) Distribution
parts:
You didn't define it for a vector, just for a real. Stan
doesn't automatically vectorize. So either you need to define
subottin_log with a vector as the first argument, or you'll have
to loop in the model block.

- Bob
